sources.title: Hasse-Schmidt derivative
sources.status: search engine retrieved substantive page; direct open returned unsupported XHTML
sources.summary: Defines multivariable Hasse derivatives over a commutative rig using a product of ordinary binomial coefficients, restricted to variables occurring in the differentiation multiset. Gives a counting interpretation as selections of occurrences. This matches the support-of-lower-index product. Historical attribution is to Hasse and Schmidt, 1937.

sources.title: Applying Koopman Methods for Nonlinear Reachability Analysis
sources.author: T.H.J. Sweering
sources.summary: Defines the multi-index binomial coefficient as the product of the ordinary coordinate binomial coefficients for nonnegative finite integer vectors with lower bounded by upper. It counts independent subset choices in the coordinates. The project totalizes this by zero when a lower coordinate exceeds its upper coordinate.

sources.title: Hasse–Schmidt derivations versus classical derivations
sources.author: Luis Narváez Macarro
sources.summary: Surveys multivariate Hasse–Schmidt derivations over arbitrary commutative algebras and recovers them from associated classical derivations in characteristic zero. This is evidence for the surrounding algebraic concept and its generality; it is not evidence that the standalone natural-number coefficient needs an independent name.

sources.title: Fast Multivariate Multipoint Evaluation over All Finite Fields
sources.status: publisher search result supplies Definition 3.4; direct DOI open forbidden (403)
sources.summary: Defines a multivariate Hasse derivative by extracting a coefficient after formal polynomial translation over a commutative ring. This is an alternative characterization of the derivative, not an alternative replacement for the scalar product alone.

sources.title: Divided powers
sources.summary: Treats axioms for divided-power structures on ideals, including binomial multiplication factors. This is related algebraic context, but it is not the definition of a two-multiindex natural-number coefficient; the project declaration does not construct a divided-power algebra.

sources.title: Higher order Leibniz rule and ordered multiindex notation
sources.summary: Distinguishes ordered lists of differentiation variables from combinatorial multiindices and gives the usual factorial quotient for their binomial coefficient under the coordinatewise order hypothesis. No new required abstraction for this scalar product follows.

sources.title: A dimension bound towards the Casas-Alvero Conjecture
sources.author: Soham Ghosh
sources.status: primary arXiv abstract opened, initial submission 2024-02-28, current v4 revised 2026-10-19
sources.summary: Uses univariate Hasse–Schmidt derivatives to formulate a current algebraic problem. This verifies recent use of the notion but supplies no more-general form of the two-multiindex coefficient.

sources.title: Analysis II: Several Variables
sources.author: Joaquim Serra
sources.status: primary lecture notes opened; relevant multiindex section inspected
sources.summary: Uses finite natural multiindices, their factorials and multinomial coefficients in Taylor formulas. Its multinomial coefficient is distinct from the product of two-index binomial coefficients, so it is not a replacement candidate.
